title: Ratios and Proportional Relationships
description: Understand ratios and unit rates; use them to solve problems.

lessons.title: Ratios and Unit Rates
lessons.content: A unit rate has a denominator of 1 and is useful for comparisons.
examples: 60 miles in 2 hours = 30 miles per hour

lessons.title: Solving Proportions
lessons.content: Set up equal ratios and solve using cross-multiplication.
examples: If 5 notebooks cost $8.75, how much do 8 cost? 5/8.75 = 8/x → x = $14

title: Percent
description: Understand percent as a ratio out of 100; apply to real-world problems.
objectives: Convert between fractions, decimals, and percents

lessons.title: Percent Conversions
lessons.content: Percent means 'per hundred'. Convert by moving the decimal or dividing by 100.

lessons.title: Percent of a Number
lessons.content: Multiply the decimal form of the percent by the number.

title: Integers and the Number Line
description: Understand negative numbers; compare, order, and use absolute value.
objectives: Represent integers on a number line

lessons.title: Negative Numbers
lessons.content: Integers extend the number line below zero.
examples: Elevation: Death Valley is −282 ft below sea level

lessons.title: Absolute Value
lessons.content: Absolute value is the distance from zero; it is always positive.

title: Operations with Integers
description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide positive and negative integers.
objectives: Add and subtract integers using rules

lessons.title: Adding and Subtracting Integers
lessons.content: Same signs: add and keep the sign. Different signs: subtract and take the sign of the larger absolute value.

lessons.title: Multiplying and Dividing Integers
lessons.content: Same signs give positive; different signs give negative.

title: Expressions and Variables
description: Write, evaluate, and simplify algebraic expressions.

lessons.title: Writing Expressions
lessons.content: Use variables to represent unknown quantities.
examples: '5 more than a number n' = n + 5

lessons.title: Evaluating and Simplifying
lessons.content: Substitute values to evaluate; combine like terms to simplify.

title: Equations and Inequalities
description: Write and solve one-step equations and inequalities.
objectives: Graph and interpret inequalities on a number line

lessons.title: One-Step Equations
lessons.content: Use inverse operations to isolate the variable.

lessons.title: Inequalities
lessons.content: An inequality has a range of solutions; graph with an open or closed circle.
examples: x > 3: open circle at 3, arrow right
x ≤ −2: closed circle at −2, arrow left

title: Area, Surface Area, and Volume
description: Calculate area of complex shapes; find surface area and volume of 3D figures.
objectives: Find area of triangles, parallelograms, and trapezoids

lessons.title: Area Formulas
lessons.content: Different shapes have specific area formulas.

lessons.title: Surface Area and Volume
lessons.content: Surface area is the total area of all faces; volume is interior space.
examples: V = lwh: a box 4×3×2 has V = 24 units³

title: Statistics — Distributions
description: Summarize data using measures of center and variability.
objectives: Find mean, median, mode, and range
Create and interpret box plots and histograms

lessons.title: Measures of Center and Spread
lessons.content: Summarize a data set with one typical value and a measure of how spread out it is.
examples: Box plot: shows minimum, Q1, median, Q3, maximum

lessons.title: Mean Absolute Deviation
lessons.content: MAD measures the average distance of each data point from the mean.

title: Geometry — Coordinate Plane
description: Use all four quadrants of the coordinate plane to solve problems.
objectives: Plot points in all four quadrants

lessons.title: Four Quadrants
lessons.content: The axes divide the coordinate plane into four quadrants.
examples: Plot (−3, 4) and (3, 4): they are reflections across the y-axis

lessons.title: Distance Between Points
lessons.content: Find horizontal or vertical distance by taking the absolute difference of the same coordinate.

title: Probability — Introduction
description: Understand basic probability concepts and calculate simple probabilities.
objectives: Define probability as a number from 0 to 1
Find the complement of an event

lessons.title: Theoretical Probability
lessons.content: P(event) = (favorable outcomes) ÷ (total outcomes)

lessons.title: Complement
lessons.content: The complement is everything that is NOT the event. P(not A) = 1 − P(A)
